descriptionChirho: Intransitive weeping or crying, expressing grief, sorrow, joy, or supplication, in all Qal finite and participial forms (bakah בָּכָה corresponds to Arabic بَكَى baka, Korean 울다, Swahili kulia).

Intensive/transitive weeping directed at or on behalf of someone, bewailing or lamenting for a person or situation, marked by Piel stem (Arabic يَبْكِينَ in intensive sense, Swahili -mlia 'weep for').
The masculine noun בֶּכִי (bekhi) denoting the act or sound of weeping as a substantive, corresponding to Arabic بُكَاء (buka'), Korean 울음, Swahili kilio.
